info.name: AeroTrace
info.description: The AeroTrace API through the api-gateway (default http://localhost:8080): the Identity Service (authentication), the Journey Service (bags, scans, journey), the Recovery Service (cases, moves, assignment, policy) the Capacity Service (resources, holds, confirmation, release) the Search Service (bag search, airport report, index status, rebuild) and the Notification Service (a handler's own notifications made from case events). Each service has its own folder; run a folder top to bottom with the runner. The gateway limits each address to about 10 requests per second (burst 20), so run with a delay of 150 ms or more between requests. Each folder signs in with the dev dummy accounts or the accounts the identity folder creates, so use the compose stack with the dev Liquibase context.

item.name: Identity Service
item.description: The authentication API of the identity-service, called through the api-gateway (default http://localhost:8080). Folders follow the API: 1 Register (passenger, staff, refusals), 2 Login, 3 Refresh token, 4 Forgot password, 5 Reset password, 6 Logout, 7 Gateway rules, 8 the identity-service on its own port. Run the whole collection top to bottom with the runner: folder 1 creates the passenger that the later folders use, and the token variables are stored in the environment by the test scripts. The gateway limits each address to about 10 requests per second (burst 20), so run with a delay of 150 ms or more between requests. Folder 1.2 signs in as adminUsername / adminPassword, which the environment sets to the dev dummy admin (dummy.admin, password dummy-password-1; created by the dev Liquibase context of the compose stack). Without that context change them, or make the first admin by hand (see the README). Every login stores its tokens in the environment (accessToken / refreshToken for the passenger, agent..., dispatcher..., newAdmin..., admin... for the others), so any request can also be run on its own.

Notification Service
item.description: The notification-service through the api-gateway: a handler's own in-app notifications, made from recovery case events. Folder 2 opens a case, moves it and assigns it to the agent through the recovery-service; the assignment event makes exactly one notification for the agent (the opening and the move have no handler, so they notify nobody). The notification is made asynchronously, so the reading requests wait about 2.5 seconds first. Everyone reads only their own notifications: another user gets an empty list and 404 for the id. Needs the compose stack with the recovery-service and the notification-service running and the dev Liquibase context (dummy accounts). Run with a delay of 150 ms or more between requests.
